ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=310357e9b0b4 introduced a refactor of ad_catalog_client.go and fetcher.go in which the fetchAdMetadata() function performs HTTP GET requests via http.DefaultClient but omits the mandatory resp.Body.Close() call after reading the response. In Go, failing to close the HTTP response body prevents the underlying TCP connection from being returned to the transport's connection pool, causing net/http.(*persistConn).readLoop and writeLoop goroutines to remain blocked indefinitely. Under normal request load this causes goroutines and file descriptors to accumulate monotonically, leading to heap exhaustion and eventual OOMKill within ~9 minutes of service start.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately restart the ad-service pod to restore service (buys ~9 minutes of operation). 2. Roll back sha=310357e9b0b4 by reverting src/ad-service/internal/client/ad_catalog_client.go and src/ad-service/internal/ads/fetcher.go to their pre-deploy state, ensuring every HTTP response body is closed with `defer resp.Body.Close()` immediately after the http.Get/Do call and before processing the body. 3. Add a static analysis lint rule (e.g., timakin/bodyclose linter) to the CI pipeline to catch missing resp.Body.Close() calls. 4. Deploy the fix and confirm goroutine count stabilizes at baseline (<100) after 10+ minutes of traffic.
